title: How is a banana this cheap?
hook_variants: This banana travelled thousands of kilometres. It costs less than a candy bar.
A banana crossed an ocean in a fridge, and it still costs pennies.
Bananas should be expensive. Here's why they're not.

scenes.say: This banana crossed an ocean in a fridge. It costs pennies.
How? Three words. Scale, ships, and green.
Picked green in Ecuador. Cooled to about thirteen degrees. Shipped north in refrigerated containers.
One refrigerated container carries over a hundred thousand bananas.
scenes.label: BANANAS PER CONTAINER

scenes.say: Then ethylene gas ripens them on cue. Shops often sell them at cost just to get you inside.
Cheap isn't magic. It's logistics at a massive scale.
Follow Landed Costs. Next time: why your coffee isn't cheap.

caption: Picked green, shipped cold, ripened with gas on demand, and often sold near cost to get you in the shop. The humble banana is a logistics masterpiece. 🍌🚢
